title: 1 Samuel Bible Quiz - Chapter 12
description: Ten questions on 1 Samuel 12: Samuel's farewell speech, his call to fear Yahweh, and the thunder and rain at wheat harvest.

questions.text: How did Samuel describe himself to all Israel?
questions.explanation: Samuel said, "I am old and gray-headed."

questions.text: What did the people answer when Samuel asked them to witness against him?
questions.explanation: They said, "You have not defrauded us, nor oppressed us, neither have you taken anything from anyone's hand."

answers.text: He had taken one ox from them
He had not defrauded or oppressed them
His sons had taken their donkeys
They would need time to think

questions.text: Whom did Samuel say Yahweh appointed to bring their fathers out of Egypt?
questions.explanation: Samuel said it is Yahweh who appointed Moses and Aaron and brought their fathers out of Egypt.

questions.text: Sisera is called the captain of the army of which place?
questions.explanation: Yahweh sold them into the hand of Sisera, captain of the army of Hazor.

questions.text: Which of these names is among those Yahweh sent to deliver Israel, according to Samuel?
questions.explanation: Yahweh sent Jerubbaal, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel and delivered them from their enemies.

questions.text: Who came against the people, so that they said, "No, but a king shall reign over us"?
questions.explanation: Samuel said that when they saw Nahash the king of the children of Ammon come against them, they said, "No, but a king shall reign over us."

answers.text: Nahash the king of the children of Ammon
Sisera, captain of the army of Hazor
The king of Moab with his army
The lords of the Philistine cities

questions.text: What did Yahweh send at wheat harvest when Samuel called to him?
questions.explanation: Samuel called to Yahweh, and Yahweh sent thunder and rain that day.

questions.text: What did the people ask Samuel to pray for?
questions.explanation: They said, "Pray for your servants to Yahweh your God, that we not die."

answers.text: That their king would be removed
That their harvest would be large

questions.text: What did Samuel say it would be a sin against Yahweh for him to do?
questions.explanation: Samuel said, "Far be it from me that I should sin against Yahweh in ceasing to pray for you."

questions.text: What did Samuel warn would happen if they kept doing evil?
questions.explanation: He said, "If you keep doing evil, you will be consumed, both you and your king."

answers.text: Only the king would be removed
Both they and their king would be consumed
They would be sent back to Egypt
